examples.text: „Bis zu den Adlerhorsten ist er den Steilhang hinuntergeklettert und hat weder Eier noch Jungvögel entdecken können.“
„Der Erzgang dieses Bergwerks … lag dicht unter der Oberfläche, sodass sie nicht über mehrere Leitern in einen tiefen Schacht hinunterzuklettern brauchten.“

glosses: An abandonment, withdrawal from, or softening of a previously expressed opinion, policy, argument, etc.

examples.text: It is interesting to speculate on what combination of factors acted within the Bush administration to bring about the climb-down from its previous position.
His climb-down from the "hard, secular" image was mainly to widen his support base.
Hours before his climb down, the premier's own cabinet ministers had vigorously defended the curriculum.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see climb, down.

examples.text: It took 2 hours to climb up, but 4 to climb down as our energy grew less and less.

glosses: To abandon, withdraw from, or soften a previously expressed opinion, argument, etc.

examples.text: But Ekeus said Iraq had climbed down in its confrontation with the UN.
No, but it may be a way for Clinton to climb down from a policy he seems increasingly to view as a no-win proposition.

If they are interested in climbing down from their oppositionism, Democrats ought to consult the Progressive Policy Institute, which has been critical of Bush, but which is developing a balanced, positive approach to the energy crisis.
